components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: Journey of water through Earth's systems

components.title: Continuous Circulation
components.subtitle: Discover how water moves constantly between the surface, atmosphere, and back again.

blocks.label: STAGE 1
blocks.title: Evaporation & Transpiration
blocks.body: The sun heats up water in oceans, rivers, and lakes, causing it to turn into vapor and rise into the air. Plants also release moisture from their leaves through transpiration.

blocks.label: STAGE 2
blocks.title: Condensation
blocks.body: As warm water vapor rises, it cools down at higher altitudes. This cooling causes the invisible gas to turn back into tiny liquid water droplets, forming clouds.

blocks.label: STAGE 3
blocks.title: Precipitation & Collection
blocks.body: When water droplets in clouds become too heavy, they fall back to Earth as rain, snow, or sleet. This water collects in oceans and rivers, restarting the entire cycle.

components.label: WORKED EXAMPLE
components.title: Tracing a Single Raindrop
components.Body: Let's follow a single molecule starting in the Pacific Ocean. It absorbs thermal energy, transforms into vapor, travels inland on jet stream winds, cools over mountain ranges, falls as fresh snow onto a glacier, melts into a rushing stream, and finally flows back to the sea.
components.takeaway: Water never truly disappears; it only changes states and location across the globe.

water_cycle_quiz.question: What process turns liquid water into water vapor in the atmosphere?
water_cycle_quiz.explanation: Evaporation is the process where heat from the sun turns liquid water into water vapor.

water_cycle_quiz.question: When water vapor cools down and turns back into liquid water droplets to form clouds, what is this called?
water_cycle_quiz.explanation: Condensation occurs when water vapor cools and changes back into liquid droplets.

water_cycle_quiz.question: Which of the following is NOT a form of precipitation?
water_cycle_quiz.explanation: Sunshine is solar radiation, whereas rain, snow, and hail are all forms of precipitation.
